summary: The broker, venue and funding channel had no adverse change this week. No Interactive Brokers outage, fee change, entity change or regulatory action dated 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-12 was found; the most recent confirmed IBKR access incident was on 2026-08-05 (APAC-hosted accounts, restored within an hour). IBKR's October metrics (released 2026-11-02) show a healthy broker: 5.678m accounts, $928.6bn client equity and margin loans of $106.8bn. No LSE trading outage was found this week, and the October UK Budget changes on stamp duty do not affect Irish-domiciled UCITS ETFs, which are already exempt. The AED/USD peg at 3.6725 is intact; the CBUAE held its base rate at 3.90% on 2026-10-28 and will very likely mirror the December Fed hike that markets now price as near-certain, which changes AED cash yields but not the conversion cost. Nothing here penalises or blocks any line.

events.issue: Channel-wide (applies to every line): IBKR October 2026 metrics show 5.678m accounts (+34% y/y), $928.6bn client equity, $106.8bn margin loans and $180.5bn credit balances. No outage, fee change or enforcement action found for 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-12. Information only.

Channel-wide (funding): the CBUAE held its base rate at 3.90% on 2026-10-28 and keeps it anchored to Fed IORB. A December Fed hike is now priced as near-certain after the hot October CPI, so a matching CBUAE hike is likely. The AED/USD peg (3.6725) is unchanged, so AED-to-USD conversion cost is unaffected; only AED cash yields move. Information only.

Venue-wide (LSE): the UK Budget will replace stamp duty on shares with a single Securities Transfer Tax from late 2027, with no rate change now. Irish-domiciled UCITS ETFs traded on the LSE are already outside UK stamp duty; whether the new tax treats them the same way should be checked once the Finance Bill 2026-27 text is published. Information only.
